inputs.value: The correct approximation for a beneficial mutation is roughly 2s (in diploids under weak selection), not 1/N.

day.reading: fixation probability and fixation rate are different quantities; 1/(2N) says nothing about when
day.holds: u is a per-mutation probability with no time unit; k = flux x u per generation; t_fix is separate

critic.reading: Bowers gives the textbook u ~ 2s for a beneficial mutation, not 1/N
critic.holds: u = 2s is correct (within 1% at 4Ns = 20; 0.1% at Day's 4Ns = 40), 40x 1/(2N) at Day's values

notes: Both statements are correct and they answer different questions: u (1/(2N) or about 2s) is a probability per new mutation; the rate is k = 2N x flux x u per generation; neither fixes when a fixation completes, which is the fixation time (4N neutral; M-601 beneficial). Day's distinction is accurate as a distinction. Whether it answers Bowers depends on which quantity the original review addressed; only Day's repost is held (BO-01 is secondhand), so the record cannot settle that.
